stem:
Lalit draws transversal $t$ across lines $p$ and $q$. A pair of corresponding angles each measures $70^\circ$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer "transversal" only, without using equal corresponding angles to test whether $p$ and $q$ are parallel.
Say that the equal $70^\circ$ measures are what create transversal $t$, instead of $t$ forming the corresponding-angle pair used in the test.
Equal corresponding angles mean $p$ and $q$ are parallel; if $p \parallel q$, corresponding angles are equal.
Treat the equal $70^\circ$ marks as vertically opposite angles only, and skip the corresponding-angles test for parallel lines.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal corresponding angles imply parallel lines, and parallel lines give equal corresponding angles. Naming only "transversal", reversing angles and transversal, or swapping in vertically opposite angles all miss that hinge.
